destination.evidence: The City requires an original signature from the property owner with the "wet" notary stamp. ... Following the virtual application submission, certain physical materials must also be mailed in or dropped off altogether to City Planning's BESt unit, including: 1. A wet-signed, notarized application form

la-alcohol-cup.notes: The process has 3 steps. Prepare the application in Simpligov. Book an 'Application Filing for Alcoholic Beverages and Dancing' appointment with DCP BESt in BuildLA (appointments.lacity.org). File at a virtual appointment, then mail or drop off the wet-signed notarized form and hard copies. The email address is for inquiries; the page does not say it accepts filings. The old address Planning.CCU@lacity.org has been discontinued. New fee rates under Ordinance 188796 took effect Feb 23, 2026, and fees are non-refundable. For Chapter 1A zoning use CP13-7773.A instead. The library calls this a 'Conditional Use Permit'. City Planning calls it a Class 2 CUP for alcohol (CUB), under LAMC 12.24 W.1. Restaurants may qualify for the Restaurant Beverage Program (CP-7850) instead.

destination.evidence: If your facility meets the reporting thresholds and is not yet enrolled, you will be required to submit a Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) through CERS. Submission of your HMBP in CERS constitutes your official application to the Los Angeles City Fire Department Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA) for the storage of hazardous materials.

la-cupa-hmbp.notes: Electronic filing only. Paper filing ended in 2013 when CERS replaced it. Plans must be updated and resubmitted every year between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Civil penalties run up to $2,000 per day, or $5,000 per day for knowing violations (HSC 25515). LAFD publishes restaurant- and grocery-specific threshold guides on the threshold page. Most restaurants only cross the threshold through CO2 for beverages or bulk cleaning chemicals. The CERS field-level questions are behind a login.

sgb-license.notes: The library URL is wrong. DocumentCenter/View/6352 is a 2016 draw.io process flowchart, not the application. San Gabriel does not post the in-city BL & Occupancy application. The city hands it out after zoning is verified (contact Community Development at (626) 308-2806 or Commdevinfo@sgch.org first). The only posted application is the Out of Town BL Application FY 25-26 (View/23679), which is for contractors and does not fit restaurants. The 2023 guide puts the general license fee at $87.75 per year, prorated quarterly. The official pages give no mailing address for new applications. Renewals go to City of San Gabriel Finance Department, 425 S. Mission Dr., San Gabriel, CA 91776. The process requires an occupancy inspection by Fire, Building and Planning before the license issues.

scaqmd-permit-lac.notes: File one Form 400-A per piece of equipment. The mailing address is printed on the form ('Mail To: SCAQMD, P.O. Box 4944, Diamond Bar, CA 91765-0944'). The library says the method is online, but the online filing system (xappprod.aqmd.gov/onlineapplicationfiling) only covers certain equipment. It includes Rule 222 registrations for charbroilers and food ovens, which matter for restaurants, plus dry cleaners and spray booths. Most other permits still go on paper Form 400-A. Under-fired charbroilers and some food ovens are registrations under Rule 222, not full permits, so check Rules 219 and 222 first. Form 400-A has not been revised since 2014.07, and its instructions date from 2010.09.

scaqmd-permit-orc.notes: This is the same form and process as scaqmd-permit-lac. South Coast AQMD covers Orange County and the urban parts of LA, Riverside and San Bernardino counties with one application. The library keeps 2 entries, one per county. Online filing covers only certain equipment, including Rule 222 charbroiler and food oven registrations. Everything else goes on paper Form 400-A (2014.07).
